fixes.explanation: Mortally ill, and Hezekiah prays. The text says, “So he prayed to the LORD, who spoke to him and gave him a sign.” (2 Chronicles 32:24) When my oven timer starts beeping in a weird way, I stand there and stare at it, and staring has never fixed one timer. Hezekiah took his problem to the right place.

Yes, the text says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). Pride was the problem, and humbling is what he does about it. I've humbled myself in front of a burnt batch before, and it's a lot cheaper than pride.

Defending is a very human move when we're caught, and I've done it over a lopsided cookie. But the text says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). Humbled is the word the verse uses.
Hiding is a very human move, and I know it well. But the verse says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). Humbled is the word, not hid.

That's right, baker. The verse says, "Then Hezekiah humbled the pride of his heart—he and the people of Jerusalem…" (2 Chronicles 32:26). The king and the people of Jerusalem both do the humbling. So the statement is false.

That's right. The verse says, "And Hezekiah prospered in all that he did." (2 Chronicles 32:30) The text says all that he did, not most of it. So struggling in most things doesn't match what the verse says.

An army is a fair guess, and a visitor who sees my ovens always asks how many cookies they bake. But the verse doesn't mention an army. It says the ambassadors were sent "…to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land…" (2 Chronicles 32:31) They came asking about a wonder, not counting soldiers.

A treaty sounds like serious grown-up business, and I'd have bet on it too. But no treaty shows up in this verse. The text says the ambassadors came "…to inquire about the wonder that had happened in the land…" (2 Chronicles 32:31) That's the only reason it gives for their visit.

That's right, baker. "…God left him alone to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart." (2 Chronicles 32:31) Test is the word the text uses. It also says what the test is for, which is all that was in Hezekiah's heart.

Protect sounds comforting, like a warm oven mitt. But the text says God left him alone "…to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart." (2 Chronicles 32:31) The verse says test, not protect.

Punish sounds heavy, and it isn't the word in the verse. The text says God left him alone "…to test him, that He might know all that was in Hezekiah’s heart." (2 Chronicles 32:31) The word there is test, so that's the one to stay with.

That's right. Hezekiah "…was buried in the upper tombs of David’s descendants." (2 Chronicles 32:33) David was Israel's king, and these tombs belong to his descendants. Hezekiah is laid to rest in those tombs.

The text puts him somewhere else. Hezekiah "…was buried in the upper tombs of David’s descendants." (2 Chronicles 32:33) No palace garden is mentioned. The burial place the text names is the upper tombs of David's descendants.
That's right, baker. "All Judah and the people of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death." (2 Chronicles 32:33) It says all Judah and the people of Jerusalem. That's a big farewell.

The text says it's true. "All Judah and the people of Jerusalem paid him honor at his death." (2 Chronicles 32:33) Honor came from all Judah, and from the people of Jerusalem too. So True is the answer.
